pages.summary: A datastore: a collection of files read a block at a time, of the kind their extensions call for.
body: The location is a file, a folder, wildcards (`'data/*.csv'`) or a list of them; text files become a `tabularTextDatastore`, spreadsheets a `spreadsheetDatastore`, images an `imageDatastore`, Parquet files a `parquetDatastore`, and MAT-files of keys and values (as `mapreduce` writes them) a key-value datastore; `'Type'` says which when the extensions do not. A datastore is a handle: `read` gives the next block and moves on, `hasdata` says whether there is more, `reset` goes back to the start, `readall` reads everything. Data too large to read at once is read this way, block by block, or through `tall` arrays and `mapreduce`.

examples.title: Three daily files read one at a time

pages.summary: Datastores of tables: delimited text files, spreadsheets and Parquet files.
body: Each file is read as `readtable` (or `parquetread`) reads it, `ReadSize` rows at a time (20000 for text, a file for spreadsheets), or a whole `'file'` (or `'sheet'`). The variable names come from the first file; `SelectedVariableNames` reads only some, and options set the delimiter, header lines and text type as `readtable`'s do. A text datastore can give timetables (`'OutputType', 'timetable'`).
syntax: Some variables, n rows at a time.

pages.summary: A datastore of images: labelled, read one by one or by number, counted and split.
body: Images are read one at a time (or `ReadSize` at a time, in a cell; `readall` gives a cell of all); `readimage` reads the k-th without moving the datastore. `'LabelSource', 'foldernames'` labels each image by its folder, as a categorical in `Labels`. `countEachLabel` gives a table of each label and how many images it has; `splitEachLabel` splits the datastore label by label, a proportion (or a number) of each label's images to each output and the rest to the last, in order unless `'randomized'`.
syntax: Labels, a read size, a function of one's own.
The k-th image, with its file and label.

pages.summary: Datastores of any files, each read by a function, and of an array in memory.
body: A `fileDatastore` reads each file by `ReadFcn` (a file name in, its data out); `'partialfile'` reads a file in pieces through [data, state, done] = f(filename, state), and `'bytes'` reads `BlockSize` bytes at a time. `readall` gives a cell, or the data joined when `UniformRead` is true. An `arrayDatastore` reads an array `ReadSize` slices at a time along `IterationDimension` (1): in a cell, or with `'OutputType', 'same'` as an array.
syntax: An array, n slices at a time.

examples.title: MAT-files read by load, and rows of a matrix

pages.summary: Everything a datastore holds; whether it has more; its first block; how far it has read.
body: `readall` reads everything from the start (tables joined one under another, images and other files in a cell), without moving the datastore. `hasdata` is true while there is more to `read`; `preview` gives the first block (eight rows of a table) without moving it; `progress` is the share read so far, from 0 to 1.

pages.summary: Datastores split into parts, put in random order, and narrowed to some files.
body: A datastore splits into parts by its files (by slices for an `arrayDatastore`): `numpartitions` says into how many (no more than a pool's workers when one is given), and `partition` gives the k-th of n parts, or the part of one file, for one worker of `parfor` each. `shuffle` puts the files (or slices) in random order, `subset` keeps some of them; `isPartitionable` and `isShuffleable` say whether a datastore can.
syntax: Some of the files or slices.
True when it can be partitioned.
True when it can be shuffled.

examples.title: A datastore of six rows, in parts

pages.summary: Datastores whose reads go through a function, and datastores written out again.
body: `transform` gives a datastore whose `read` gives what a function makes of the original's read (one input for each datastore given; with `'IncludeInfo'` the function takes and gives the info too). `writeall` reads each file and writes it to a folder again (tables by `writetable`, images by `imwrite`, other data to MAT-files), the folders under the files' common folder kept unless `'FolderLayout'` is `'flatten'`, with a prefix or suffix to the names.

examples.title: Tables cleaned on the way in, and written out

pages.summary: Map and reduce functions run over a datastore.
body: `mapreduce` reads the datastore block by block and calls the map function on each, `mapfun(data, info, intermKVStore)`, which adds keys and values with `add` (one) or `addmulti` (several). Then it calls the reduce function once for each key, `reducefun(key, valueIterator, outKVStore)`, which reads that key's values with `hasnext` and `getnext` and adds its results. The result is a key-value datastore: `readall` gives a table of Key and Value. With `'OutputFolder'` the results are saved there too.

examples.title: Totals by group, in two passes
examples.intro: The map function totals each block by group; the reduce function adds up each group's totals.

pages.summary: Tall arrays: computations on data too large for memory, done when gathered.
body: `tall` makes a tall array of an array or of a datastore. Operators, indexing (`t(k)`, `t.Var`, `t{:, 'x'}`) and the common functions of numbers, tables, text, dates and categories give tall arrays that remember what to compute; `gather` computes it, each step once, reading a datastore block by block. A value that is not tall is given back as it is. `istall` says whether a value is tall; `classUnderlying` gives the class of its values and `isaUnderlying` tests it (also for `'numeric'`, `'float'` or `'integer'`). Plots of tall arrays gather them first.
syntax: A tall array of an array.
True when its values are of a class.

examples.title: A mean over files, computed when gathered
examples.code:
mkdir parts
for k = 1:4
    writetable(table(k*(1:5)', 'VariableNames', {'x'}), sprintf('parts/p%d.csv', k));
end
t = tall(tabularTextDatastore('parts'));
m = mean(t.x)
istall(m)
gather(m)
[classUnderlying(t.x), string(isaUnderlying(t.x, 'float'))]
[lo, hi] = gather(min(t.x), max(t.x))
